summary: The user writes in German (casual, with typos) and expects answers in German. Code, identifiers, comments, scripts and developer docs must be English; UI text stays German.

The user rejected a bloated first UI (dashboard, status badges, placeholder cards). Every visible element must have a concrete purpose; no UI for future features. The app should feel like a tool, not a project dashboard.
The user sends structured work orders (German markdown). Save each one unchanged to workspace/docs/build-orders/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>.md.

The user also sends short ideas in chat (e.g. the rhyme canvas). Build them pragmatically, document your own decisions in workspace/docs/decisions.md and list open choices instead of asking many questions up front.
Go 1.27 + Wails v2.17.1 + SQLite (modernc.org/sqlite, pure Go, no CGO). Plain HTML/CSS/JS ES modules in frontend/dist, no npm, no framework.
First build order: full 7-area UI (A01-A07) with status badges, EXE, desktop shortcut, dev/build/shortcut scripts, README. Later replaced by the UI reduction.

Navigation reduced to Reimarchiv (active), Reimzeilen (planned), Generator (planned), Einstellungen (active). Planned areas render a one-line page; areas without a view file are planned automatically.

Functional rhyme archive: add a word with a user-assigned vowel class (a/e/i/o/u) and optional rhyme sound (sound sequence from the stressed vowel), live search over word and rhyme sound, vowel filter with counts, list grouped by rhyme sound, two-click delete, case-insensitive duplicate check including umlauts (via a lowercased key column).

Google-Maps-like dark canvas below the list: pan by dragging the background, wheel zoom at the cursor (30-200 %), 'Einpassen' (fit all), one movable/resizable window per vowel class, z-order, close, splitter for the pane height. Layout persisted in SQLite ui_state (key 'rhymes.canvas') with a 400 ms debounce.
SQLite at %APPDATA%\LykosReimarchiv\reimarchiv.db, schema v3 via an append-only migrations list and PRAGMA user_version: v1 app_meta, v2 words, v3 ui_state. Never edit an existing migration.

App log at %APPDATA%\LykosReimarchiv\logs\app.log, opened in App.startup (not in main) so the Wails binding-generation run during builds doesn't write to it. Build logs go to workspace/logs/build-*.log (gitignored).

Created workspace/ as the shared root for the user and the CLI: docs/ (start-draft.md moved here, decisions.md, build-orders/), state/ (STATE.md, this Handoff.jsonl), logs/ (sessions/*.md, build logs). CLAUDE.md at the repo root holds the rules.
go test ./... covers storage: migrations and reopen, word validation and normalisation, duplicates incl. umlauts, list/filter/search incl. literal LIKE wildcards, counts, delete, UI state.

scripts/build.ps1 [-Shortcut] builds packaging\bin\LykosReimarchiv.exe and refuses to run while the app is open. scripts/create-shortcut.ps1 creates 'LYKOS REIMARCHIV.lnk' on the desktop (exists and points to the EXE). scripts/dev.ps1 runs wails dev.
First commit of the whole project pushed to origin/main (https://github.com/LYKOS68/lyricforce). Before this, the repo had no commits and the remote was empty.

Agreed rhyme roadmap from start-draft.md: 1) monosyllables and simple vowels (current), 2) diphthongs /aɪ̯/ /aʊ̯/ /ɔʏ̯/, 3) multisyllabic and end rhymes, 4) syllable analysis and metric filters, 5) Reimzeilen (relatable lines) and contrast generator, 6) full search system.

Rhyme logic is phonetic, never orthographic. 'ie' is not a diphthong but spells /iː/. Rhymes are determined by the sound sequence from the stressed vowel. Sound classes are extended step by step without replacing the core logic. Don't add spelling-based vowel detection.

workspace/docs/reime.txt is the user's own rhyme collection (87 lines, mostly A-vowel rhymes: monosyllables, two-syllable and multisyllabic rhymes, word combinations, separated by ' / '). It was added by the user, not generated. It's a natural seed/import source for the archive, but importing needs the user's OK and decisions on vowel/rhyme-sound assignment, since the archive is phonetic and the file is plain spelling. The user agreed to publish it in the public repo.
Only Reimarchiv is in active development. Reimzeilen and Generator stay one-line navigation targets until the user starts them.

The first UI (dashboard, status badges, placeholder cards for all 7 areas) followed the first order literally, but the user found it bloated and ordered a reduction. Lesson: prefer minimal, functional UI and don't pre-build future features.
The existing .gitignore rule 'dist/' would have excluded frontend/dist, which is source code here. Fixed with '!frontend/dist/'. Watch out for this when changing ignore rules.

A build failed with 'Access is denied' because the running app locked the EXE. build.ps1 now aborts with a clear message. Once I force-closed the user's running (old) app instance to rebuild; ask before doing that again.
Wails runs the compiled program once during 'Generating bindings', which wrote fake 'start' lines into the user's app.log. Fixed by opening the log file in App.startup.

No Chrome/Edge browser is installed (no headless browser tests). sqlite3 isn't on PATH in bash or pwsh: use a throwaway Go program that imports internal/storage, placed in a tmp/ dir that you delete afterwards. SetForegroundWindow is blocked, so screenshots use PrintWindow (flag 2) on the app window. Long bash heredocs with mixed quotes can fail: write helper scripts to the scratchpad with the Write tool instead.

UI Automation works with WebView2: ValuePattern.SetValue on inputs, SelectionItemPattern on radios, InvokePattern on buttons/links. Elements with visibility:hidden are absent from the UIA tree (the delete button was switched to opacity for this reason and for keyboard access). Mouse drags work via PostMessage WM_LBUTTONDOWN/WM_MOUSEMOVE/WM_LBUTTONUP to the child window 'Chrome_RenderWidgetHostHWND' (client offset 8,31 in the screenshot). Posted WM_MOUSEWHEEL is ignored.

Not verified by script: wheel zoom on the canvas (only indirectly, through real wheel/touchpad input from the user arriving during tests) and resizing canvas windows at the corner. The user was asked to try the resize corner.

All UI tests ran against the user's real database in %APPDATA%. Test words were deleted and the canvas state was reset to '{}' afterwards. Next time consider a separate data dir for tests, e.g. an env var override in internal/appdir.
Ask the user how the canvas feels in practice (zoom speed, accidental zoom from a touchpad, window sizes) before extending it.
Decide with the user: restrict the archive to monosyllables for now, or store a syllable count?

Decide the rhyme sound notation: free text vs. IPA vs. a fixed sound inventory. Also short vs. long vowel (/a/ vs. /aː/) as its own field or as part of the rhyme sound. This shapes the future phonetic engine.
Editing an existing word (currently only add and delete).
Optional, not decided: windows per rhyme sound (e.g. '-acht'), keyboard controls, windows that follow the list search/filter.
Export, import and backup were removed from Einstellungen in the reduction. Only add them back once they actually work.

At the end of every session: update workspace/state/STATE.md, append to workspace/logs/sessions/<date>.md, write handoff lines for the next model into workspace/state/Handoff.jsonl, and commit/push only if the user asks.
